acceptance_criteria.criterion: The append-only scoreboard contains 2–3 comparable, explicitly assigned runs for every arm used in the final A/B/C/D comparison, including the remaining C samples.

An E3 run declares its charter-freshness hypothesis and kill signal before launch, then records cost, premise failures, review repair load, 72-hour escapes, wall-clock, ledger honesty, and qualitative grade.

The synthesis ranks arms by tokens per merged slice only among candidates whose premise-failure and 72-hour escape rates remain quality-equivalent to A; uncertainty and incomparable samples are called out rather than averaged away.
Every rejected arm or E hypothesis records why it lost and which omitted research or review control would have caught each observed failure earlier.

The winning controls are implemented in bp-epic-cycle.workflow.js with the invariant merge gates, security auto-escalation, premise verification, evidence stamping, and improvement-only rule preserved.
A focused workflow test or reproducible dry-run proves the graduated configuration selects the intended research depth and review shape without weakening existing required gates.

purpose.statement: Finish the A/B/C/D/E epic-cycle experiment and graduate only the research and review controls that preserve quality at lower cost.
purpose.why: The larger epic-cycle improvement goal is to spend fewer tokens and less wall-clock time without increasing false premises, repair load, or 72-hour escapes. Existing samples suggest broad survey work may be expensive dead weight, but the C arm, E3 hypothesis, cross-arm ranking, and workflow graduation are incomplete. Completing those controlled comparisons is the right intervention because only comparable runs with a fixed quality floor can distinguish a cheaper method from a merely under-measured one. If omitted, Barkpark either keeps paying for research that adds no value or removes safeguards on anecdote and silently lowers the merge bar.
